---
title: "Quiz: Zernike moments on the unit disc"
---

Short questions to test your understanding. Try each on paper first, then open the answer. $V_{nm} = R_{nm}(\rho)e^{im\theta}$ on the unit disc ($n - |m|$ even, $|m| \le n$); $Z_{nm} = \frac{n+1}{\pi}\iint I\,\overline{V_{nm}}$; $\theta$ counter-clockwise.

---

**Q1.** Which $(n, m)$ are allowed for $n = 3$? How many zeros does $R_{31}$ have inside the disc ($0 < \rho < 1$)?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$|m| \le n$ and $n - |m|$ even; $R_{nm}$ has $(n - |m|)/2$ zeros.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$m = -3, -1, 1, 3$. $R_{31} = 3\rho^3 - 2\rho$ has $(3-1)/2 = 1$ zero inside: $\rho = \sqrt{2/3} = 0.816$.
:::

---

**Q2.** Why is the radial part orthogonal with the weight $\rho$, i.e. $\int_0^1 R_{nm}R_{n'm}\,\rho\,d\rho$, and not with $d\rho$ alone?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What is the area element in polar coordinates?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The polynomials must be orthogonal on the disc as an area: $dx\,dy = \rho\,d\rho\,d\theta$. After the angular integral, the factor $\rho$ remains. A ring of radius $\rho$ has circumference $2\pi\rho$, so outer rings count more.
:::

---

**Q3.** An image is rotated by 30° counter-clockwise. What happens to $Z_{22}$, $Z_{31}$ and $Z_{40}$?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$Z_{nm} \to Z_{nm}e^{-im\alpha}$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
All keep their magnitude. The phase of $Z_{22}$ changes by $-60°$, of $Z_{31}$ by $-30°$, and $Z_{40}$ (real, $m = 0$) does not change at all.
:::

---

**Q4.** A real image has $Z_{42} = 0.3 - 0.1i$. What is $Z_{4,-2}$? Why is it enough to store the moments with $m \ge 0$?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$\overline{V_{nm}} = V_{n,-m}$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$Z_{4,-2} = \overline{Z_{42}} = 0.3 + 0.1i$. For a real image every $Z_{n,-m}$ is the conjugate of $Z_{nm}$, so the negative $m$ carry no extra information.
:::

---

**Q5.** A classifier uses $|Z_{nm}|$ for $n \le 8$ to recognise digits in any orientation. Which two digits will it confuse, and why can't more orders fix it?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Which digit is another one rotated?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
6 and 9: a 9 is (nearly) a 6 rotated by 180°, and all magnitudes are exactly rotation invariant, at every order. More orders add more invariants, but every one of them is blind to rotation. One needs a non-invariant feature (a phase, or the upright orientation).
:::

---

**Q6.** Why should the disc be centred on the object's centroid before computing Zernike moments?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What is $Z_{11}$ in terms of $m_{10}$ and $m_{01}$?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Zernike moments are only rotation invariant for rotations about the disc's centre; moving the object changes all of them. Centring the disc on the centroid makes them translation invariant (and $Z_{11} = \frac2\pi(m_{10} - im_{01}) = 0$). Scaling the radius to the object's size makes them scale invariant.
:::

---

**Q7.** A Zernike reconstruction of a micrograph is very good inside the disc but has a large error over the whole square image. Why?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Where are the $V_{nm}$ defined?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The basis lives on the inscribed disc: the corners (21 % of the square) are not described at all, so the reconstruction is 0 there. For a shape that lies inside the disc on a dark background this does not matter; for a crop of a larger image it does.
:::

---

**Q8.** Computing $R_{40,0}(\rho)$ with the factorial formula gives values that are wrong by up to 0.015, although every term is computed accurately. Why?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
How large are the individual terms compared with the result?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The terms alternate in sign and the largest is about $5 \times 10^{13}$, while the sum is at most 1. Each term carries a relative rounding error of about $10^{-16}$, i.e. an absolute error up to about $10^{-2}$, which survives the cancellation. A recurrence in $n$ never forms such large terms.
:::

---

**Q9.** *(math)* Show that $\int_0^1 R_{20}R_{00}\,\rho\,d\rho = 0$ and compute $\int_0^1 R_{20}^2\,\rho\,d\rho$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$R_{20} = 2\rho^2 - 1$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
$\int_0^1 (2\rho^3 - \rho)\,d\rho = \tfrac12 - \tfrac12 = 0$. $\int_0^1 (2\rho^2 - 1)^2\rho\,d\rho = \int_0^1 (4\rho^5 - 4\rho^3 + \rho)\,d\rho = \tfrac23 - 1 + \tfrac12 = \tfrac16 = \frac{1}{2(n+1)}$ for $n = 2$.
:::
